sourceFiles.excerpt: The right choice starts with the finished part rather than the label on the spool.

example.description: Walk through the tracked part-first material rule against an explicitly fictional 65°C clamp requirement.
example.demonstration: The tracked MooreCode guide says to start with the finished part. The post applies that rule to a stated 65°C service requirement, compares it with fetched manufacturer values, and labels the result as a paper screen rather than a physical test.
example.calculation: No worker arithmetic is requested for this source walkthrough. The post separately shows the manufacturer-value screens: 60 - 65 = -5°C for the named PLA and 68 - 65 = 3°C for the named PETG.
example.excerpt: The existing MooreCode filament guide puts the decision in one sentence: “The right choice starts with the finished part rather than the label on the spool.” After a failure, that rule keeps me from reaching for a popular filament before I can name what the old part failed to do.
example.claimLimits: The tracked source supports the selection method, not a tested clamp, customer result, universal material ranking, or promise that a particular spool, geometry, print profile, or orientation will survive 65°C under load.

references.sourceExcerpt: Parts start to lose mechanical strength at temperatures over 60 °C.
references.supportingClaim: Prusament says its PLA parts start to lose mechanical strength above 60°C.
references.primarySourceRationale: Prusament manufactures the named PLA and this final public HTTPS material page directly returns the quoted temperature warning in fetched HTML. It supports only the named product's paper screen, not a finished clamp result.

references.supportingClaim: Prusament lists 68°C temperature resistance for its PETG
references.primarySourceRationale: Prusament manufactures the compared PETG, and this final public HTTPS page directly returns both its PLA comparison and the 68 °C product detail in fetched HTML. The catalog value supports the three-degree paper margin only; it does not certify the fictional clamp under sustained load.

references.sourceExcerpt: Soft and bendable at thin layers, strong and durable at thick layers
references.supportingClaim: Prusament lists TPU 95A as “Soft and bendable at thin layers, strong and durable at thick layers.”
references.primarySourceRationale: Prusament manufactures TPU 95A and this final public HTTPS material page directly returns the quoted thickness-dependent description in fetched HTML. It supports only that named filament, not settings or behavior for every TPU.

claimRationale: The exact tracked MooreCode excerpt supports choosing from the finished part's requirement and does not establish a live test. The fictional requirement is 65°C. Directly fetched Prusament text supplies the 60°C PLA warning and 68°C PETG catalog value, so the post correctly reports 60 - 65 = -5°C and 68 - 65 = 3°C. Those screening margins support rejecting the named PLA on paper and testing the named PETG next; they do not prove service life for another product, geometry, profile, orientation, time, or load. The TPU excerpt applies only to Prusament TPU 95A.
